diagnosis.surface: H-pub (committed run_cell cell machinery — the agent-deadline-lapse / cell-teardown leg)
diagnosis.root_cause: crates/hh-helper/src/podman.rs — `PodmanBackend::terminate_group` ran `podman exec <ctr> pkill -TERM -f <pat>` then `pkill -KILL -f <pat>` inside the cell. `pkill` ships with procps, which is absent on the podman guest's minimal task-env image — the exec failed rc 127 (`pkill: not found`), the cell could not terminate its agent subprocess, and the slot recorded a verbatim `cell-terminate` machinery exception (`verifier_unavailable`-class). Wc2's re-proof (PR #367, 8e425dd5) observed it on 3 H-pub cells; the real trials otherwise landed (O R/R 9/10, H-pub R/R 6/9). A second latent failure stood next to it: `pkill` exits 1 on no-match, so an agent that already exited between lapse and terminate recorded the no-match rc as a machinery error too.
diagnosis.why_not_podman_top: `podman top <ctr> hpid` reports *guest-VM* PIDs — a host-side `kill` cannot reach them across podman-machine/remote, and `podman kill` would stop the whole cell whose verify legs still run. The kill must execute inside the cell.

repair.scope: machinery only — `PodmanBackend::terminate_group` in crates/hh-helper/src/podman.rs; the drawn tasks, surfaces O/H-pub/H-allow, the R/R admit rule and the committed replacement orders are untouched; no new record kind or schema; the CellOps signature is unchanged
repair.act: `pkill` replaced by an in-cell `/proc` cmdline walk: `podman exec -e HH_KILL_PAT=<pat> -e HH_KILL_SIG=<TERM|KILL> <ctr> sh -c <walk>` — for every `/proc/[0-9]*/cmdline`, `grep -q -E -e "$HH_KILL_PAT"` matches the ERE against the raw cmdline bytes (the same string `pkill -f` saw) and the POSIX `kill -s` builtin signals the pid. Only `sh`, `grep`, `/proc`, and the `kill` builtin are required — all present on the minimal Debian base layers (procps is not). The pattern rides env, not argv: the walker's own cmdline never contains the pattern value (no self-match, no argv quoting). `$$` is excluded for good measure. The TERM pass stays best-effort and the KILL pass's exec result stays authoritative (an unreachable cell is still a typed machinery error); an empty pattern refuses before argv, and a no-match pass is success — the goal, no surviving match, is met.
repair.callers: crates/hh-runner/src/cell.rs `PodmanCell::terminate_group` (run_cell ST3 lapse + exec deadline lapse) and crates/hh-runner/src/bin/hh_w1.rs — both forward unchanged to the repaired backend method
